title: Qt: Speed up ProtoTreeModel with lots of items
description:
When creating a ProtoNode, count the (non-hidden) children and put
them in a QVector. This saves time having to iterate through all
of a node's children (or the parent's children) each time the
model or view wants to get the row or index number. Create and
delete the needed ProtoNodes when the root node is changed, instead
of recreating them on demand from the proto_nodes (since they're no
longer a thin wrapper.)

Fix #18625

notes.body: @desowin, I'm not a Qt expert, but this makes it instantaneous to expand the item list on frame 2026140 in that file of yours, by changing the index function (and several others, like rowCount, and others implicitly like hasChildren) to O(1).

> Create the ProtoNodes persistantly

Presumably "persistently" doesn't mean "we keep, in memory, a full tree for every packet in the file until the file is closed".

> Presumably "persistently" doesn't mean "we keep, in memory, a full tree for every packet in the file until the file is closed".

No, only for the duration the protocol tree is displayed. When you switch to another packet, the old one is freed and new one is allocated.

No, it means that they're all created when the root node of the model is changed (i.e., the packet is changed), and when that happens the set for the previous packet are deleted. That keeps the memory increase from being too much.

The current implementation traverses the C proto_tree directly and creates a new C++ ProtoNode wrapper around a proto_node each time one is accessed. Determining the number of children each time is what is slow currently.

When optimizing for large number of children, it is worthwhile to consider doing 2 traversals over the list. The first pass would be used solely to calculate the number of elements, then the list would be preallocated with the count (`m_children.reserve(count);`) and populated on the second traversal.

That way, the list will only be as large as needed (i.e. no empty slots), and there will be only one allocation instead of multiple reallocations that are currently happening when appending elements.
Makes sense.

Ah, I see where those are. All the places in `ProtoTree` that call `protoNodeFromIndex(idx)->protoNode()` need to check if the return value for `protoNodeFromIndex()` is a null pointer. Previously as it wasn't a pointer, it would return a value whose `.protoNode()` member was null.

And it is trivial to reproduce. For example using the capture from #18625, navigate to frame 199 (GET DESCRIPTOR Response DEVICE), expand the DEVICE DESCRIPTOR in packet tree, then click on frame 198 and observe the crash. Frame 198 contains only USB Link Layer, while frame 199 contains USB Link Layer, USB URB and DEVICE DESCRIPTOR.

Almost all the public accesses of that function are cases where `protoNodeFromIndex(idx)` is immediately followed by a call to `->protoNode()` of that `protoNode()`, and they can handle when the `proto_node*` returned is NULL. Probably simplest to replace the call in `ProtoTreeModel` with something that directly returns the `proto_node*` and returns NULL if the ProtoNode is NULL.
And most of those are just passing it to construct a `FieldInformation`, so maybe _that_ should just have a constructor that takes a `ProtoNode*` instead of just one that takes a `proto_node*`

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/8837/diffs?diff_id=531763401&start_sha=3823c6262d9a3d383dfb2e29b522370787c155c3#6d973ab1ed4d54d26e69b4c965288a463af4f975_702_703)

This destroys the all objects returned by `ProtoNode::child()`, this might not be a problem, but it puts quite big lifetime restriction on the returned child elements. Can the `m_children` be changed to mere `proto_node *` lookup table?

I initially tried that, and I found that I was still having to loop through the node children in order to count them many times. Maybe there's a better way.

It might be possible to defer the children counting and creation until a node is expanded in the tree view, using `fetchMore`.
Deferring with `fetchMore` most likely won't resolve the issue I am concerned about. The thing is, can `ProtoNode::child()` pointer outlive its parent? If not, then there is no problem at all.

I don't think so, because it's only destroyed when the root node is changed, and the calls to `beginResetModel()` are supposed to tell the callers that all the existing `QModelIndex`es are invalid and not to use them. After making the other fix I haven't been able to trigger an issue on a ASAN build so far.
requested review from @rknall
Small point, using a QVector here instead of a QList might even improve facts further.
Apparently "QVector<T> used to be a different class in Qt 5, but is now a simple alias to QList," but I think you're right, using a QVector might be better for Qt 5.

changed this line in [version 3 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/8837/diffs?diff_id=531766178&start_sha=bd456ad572968160d83c8f47a92bb3832869bbd1#6745267c90ecf907f65f1d2e26b823a45f7a0698_60_56)
Yes, that was my thinking. It does not matter for Qt6, but for anyone still building with Qt5 it is quite a difference

The Iterator should in theory be as fast. And also, the improvement seems to be coming from the fact that the isValid() is not being used. But it should be used, as otherwise invalid items may be used?
I may be overlooking something, but the only real improvement seems to be for me getting rid of the Iterator and instead presenting a finite for-loop. Or am I missing something here?

The iterator should in theory be as fast as anything. I was considering rewriting it to use the QList (or QVector), in which case there's no need to test isValid() because validity is tested when inserting children into the QList - because the indices into the list need to match the valid items and skip the invalid (hidden) items. But it's probably not a huge speedup, you're right, and may not be necessary to do.

I'll change this code in packet_diagram back in the next version, whether I change the iterator or not.

I removed the iterator temporarily so that I could see where the code failed to compile without the iterator, and see which uses of the iterator really wanted to find the child at a known index and could be replaced with calls accessing the List/Vector. This one in `packet_diagram` truly does need to iterate over all the children though.

It seems that this change makes Wireshark to clear the protocol tree items expanded state on packet change. That is, open any capture file with atleast 2 frames, expand any tree item in frame 1, switch to frame 2 and then back to frame 1. Notice that the expanded state is not preserved and instead all items are collapsed.

Yes, that's what the part in `proto_tree.cpp` around line 443 that is `ifdef`'ed out is for. That's the one thing I know I need to resolve. Right now it's part of parsing the `proto_tree` directly, so it needs to search for the `QModelIndex` that corresponds with that `proto_node`, which could be slow.

I'm thinking of implementing a function in `ProtoTreeModel` to do the foreach search there.
Found a good way to handle it, fixed in the latest version.
